source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies a hidden recanting witness, imposes proxy restrictions, completeness of Z for the witness, and two outcome-bridge equations; Proposition 3.1 lifts them to latent equations and Theorem 3.1 identifies E[Y(M2(M1(0),1),M1(0),0)].

The paper has observed recanting witness D and distinct latent U; Assumption 5 specifies Z and W proxies, Assumption 6 gives three Z-completeness conditions, and Theorem 2.1 identifies E[Y(1,D(1),M(0,D(1)))] through h2,h1,h0.

Theorem 4 derives an inductive interventional margin under sequential proxy independence, fixing ignorability, bridge existence, sequential completeness, and positivity; Section 5.3 states that completeness of Proximal ID remains open.

The journal article studies counterfactual-mean functionals with nonunique proximal bridge solutions, distinguishes functional identification from root-n estimability, and develops inference under additional conditions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Promote the calibrated theorem, rather than the conditional envelope, as the sole headline and state formally that its model class contains a named rank-deficient success law excluded by Wu--Bai--Cui Assumption 3.2.

Give a generic finite-dimensional family of positive rank-deficient calibrated laws satisfying the loading condition, with the rational artifact as one member, rather than relying on one exact success SCM.

Develop the full-law converse into either a generic-class obstruction or a maximal observable subclass theorem; this would turn the present sufficient singleton result into a genuine identification frontier.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the calibrated subclass as the field-tier kernel and retain the conditional envelope only under its accepted scope caveat.
